requirements.assessment: Official component requirement, not merely EMI optimization wording.
Official recommendation, not worded as must; still a sensible selection threshold for replacements.

requirements.item: Polarity marking and prescribed physical layout orientation, Fig28/Fig26
requirements.short_exact_quote: The inductor must be marked for polarity
requirements.assessment: Explicit reference-design requirement; no-mark parts do not satisfy it merely because inductance/current ratings match.
Specific brand/MPN is a recommendation; alternative manufacturers are not categorically forbidden.
Efficiency/performance recommendation. Larger saturation-current headroom is generally better; original 2.4 A is not a mandatory numerical threshold.

The documented reason is leakage-field interaction with the VREG_LX-inductor-COUT loop, affecting regulation/control loop and output voltage, especially at high output current and high load transients. It is not framed solely as radiated EMI reduction.

inductor_requirements.decision: No-mark generic parts are unqualified as production drop-in substitutes under the official design requirements. This does not prove they cannot operate. An exception would need an explicit engineering deviation plus startup, line/load/transient/temperature and winding-orientation variation qualification; that validation is not provided by catalog checks or package geometry.
inductor_requirements.scope_limit: No supplier contact, transaction, qualification test or PCB edit performed. Exact approved Abracon part and official reference geometry remain the lower-risk design pending supply resolution.

guide.finding: Incorrect winding orientation affects output capacitor coupling and internal control circuitry. Other layouts/components might tolerate either direction but likely need more PCB area; deviations from example are at designer risk.

requirements.wording_note: Polarity is a must, not merely EMI optimization: official text ties leakage field orientation to control-loop/output-voltage operation under high load/transients. Current minimum uses should. Latest official section6.3.8.3, printed456, figure25; older local source section6.3.8.2/3 printed451/452 figure24.
